verified_facts.text: The hotel is in Vienna's first district, directly on the Ringstrasse (Ring Boulevard).
verified_facts.excerpt: is located in the beautiful first district of the world capital of music, directly on the famous Ringstrasse (Ring Boulevard).

verified_facts.text: The building was originally a private palace built for Duke Philipp of Wuerttemberg.
verified_facts.excerpt: Originally built as a private residence of Duke Philipp of Württemberg, the Palais on Vienna’s Ring Boulevard was transformed into the Hotel Imperial

verified_facts.text: Duke Philipp of Wuerttemberg had the palace built in 1863 as a token of his love for his wife, Archduchess Marie Therese.
verified_facts.excerpt: In 1863 Duke Philipp of Wuerttemberg had today’s Hotel Imperial built as a token of his love for his wife, Archduchess Marie Therese.

verified_facts.text: Interiors feature marble, hand-carved statues and crystal chandeliers.
verified_facts.excerpt: The interior furnishings of the Hotel Imperial subtly showcase the 19th century romance of Vienna with pristine marble, hand-carved statues, and dazzling crystal chandeliers.

verified_facts.text: The Royal Staircase in the lobby leads up to the rooms and suites beneath chandeliers and high stucco ceilings.
verified_facts.excerpt: Inside the lobby, the Royal Staircase leading up to the suites and rooms is illuminated by magnificent chandeliers that sparkle and shine from high stucco ceilings imbued with aristocratic flair.

verified_facts.text: Rooms and suites are appointed with original paintings, antiques, stucco ceilings and fine fabrics.
verified_facts.excerpt: appointed with original paintings, antiques, stucco ceilings and fine fabrics

verified_facts.text: Rooms are furnished with authentic antiques, silk-covered walls and marble bathrooms.
verified_facts.excerpt: Tastefully furnished with precious, authentic antiques, walls cocooned in silk, and bathrooms made of marble

verified_facts.text: The Royal Suites were once the private apartments of Prince Philipp of Wuerttemberg, with crystal chandeliers on seven-metre stucco ceilings.
verified_facts.excerpt: Today’s Royal Suites were once the private apartments of Prince Phillipp of Wuerttemberg. Crystal chandeliers gleam from seven metre stucco ceilings

verified_facts.text: Private balconies offer views over the roofs and spires of old Vienna.
verified_facts.excerpt: Private balconies offer splendid views of the roofs and spires of old Vienna

verified_facts.text: The Sisi Suites are named after Empress Sisi.
verified_facts.excerpt: Since Vienna and the most famous former Empress Sisi are inseparable, we have honored her with a beautiful room category that we named after her.

verified_facts.text: A private butler service is available on request.
verified_facts.excerpt: A private butler service is even available on request

verified_facts.text: There are three Clefs d'Or concierges on the hotel team.
verified_facts.excerpt: There are three Clefs d’Or concierges in the Hotel Imperial team.

verified_facts.text: The Imperial Torte was created to mark the hotel's opening, in honour of Emperor Franz Josef I, and its recipe is still a secret.
verified_facts.excerpt: The cake was created to mark the opening of the Hotel Imperial and in honour of Emperor Franz Josef I. Of course the recipe is a well-kept secret to this day.

verified_facts.text: Café Imperial Wien serves Viennese classics such as Tafelspitz, Wiener Schnitzel and the handmade Imperial Torte.
verified_facts.excerpt: The gracefully restored Café Imperial Wien is a historic landmark serving international and Viennese culinary classics, from traditional "Tafelspitz" and one of the city's finest "Wiener Schnitzel" to the renowned handmade "Imperial Torte".

verified_facts.text: Afternoon tea is served daily in the Imperial Bar.
verified_facts.excerpt: Enjoy an exquisite Imperial Afternoon Tea in our majestic Imperial Bar, offering exclusive teas, exquisite scones, and savory as well as sweet delicacies.

verified_facts.text: The Imperial Bar, once an open courtyard, became the grand Imperial Bar in 2014.
verified_facts.excerpt: Originally built as an open courtyard, this radiant area was transformed into a Restaurant for the Vienna’s World Fair, later into the Hotel Lobby (as pictured), and in 2014 into the grand Imperial Bar.

verified_facts.text: Alfred Hitchcock, Charlie Chaplin and Richard Wagner are among the hotel's past guests.
verified_facts.excerpt: Alfred Hitchcock searches his wife in his spacious suite, Charlie Chaplin lives as imperially as never before, while Richard Wagner resides in seven rooms.

verified_facts.text: Sigmund Freud, Gustav and Alma Mahler and Stefan Zweig took their coffee at the hotel's coffee house.
verified_facts.excerpt: Sigmund Freud, Gustav and Alma Mahler as well as Stefan Zweig order their coffee and "their" newspaper here.

verified_facts.text: Housekeeping is provided twice daily.
verified_facts.excerpt:
Housekeeping

Twice Daily

verified_facts.text: The hotel has 2 Michelin Keys.
verified_facts.excerpt: 2 Michelin Keys for Hotel Imperial, 2025 by Michelin Guide

verified_facts.text: The hotel was named to Conde Nast Traveler's 2024 Gold List.
verified_facts.excerpt: Hotel Imperial, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Vienna is recognized in Condé Nast Traveler’s 2024 Gold List.

verified_facts.text: Parking is off-site; the concierge recommends nearby underground garages.
verified_facts.excerpt: If you wish to park in an underground garage, our Concierge will be happy to recommend one in the vicinity of the hotel.

verified_facts.text: There are no electric vehicle charging stations at the hotel.
verified_facts.excerpt: No, Hotel Imperial, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Vienna does not have electric vehicle charging stations.

verified_facts.text: Pets are welcome, with dog amenities including a bowl, bed and welcome kit.
verified_facts.excerpt: and provide the following amenities for their comfort: a dog bowl, bed and mat, and a Pet Welcome Kit.

verified_facts.text: The nearest subway station is Karlsplatz.
verified_facts.excerpt:
Subway Station

Karlsplatz
